description_ru: В лондонской гостинице Дэниел открывает чужой чемодан с красным платьем. Забавная история о перепутанном багаже и новой дружбе.
text:
Daniel arrived at Gatwick airport on a Thursday evening after a long flight from Toronto. He was tired and hungry, and he wanted only a hot shower and a bed. He waited at the baggage belt for twenty minutes, and at last he saw his blue suitcase. He pulled it off the belt, said a quiet thank you and walked out to the taxi stand.

The hotel was in the centre of London. When Daniel opened his suitcase in his room, he got a terrible shock. There were no shirts, no jeans and no laptop. Instead, he found a red dress, three pairs of high shoes, a big bag of sweets and a thick book called "Learn Italian in Thirty Days". The suitcase looked exactly like his, but it was not his. On the handle there was a small label with a name: Carla Rossi, Milan.

He sat on the bed and put his head in his hands. Tomorrow morning he had an important presentation, and his notes were on his laptop, and his laptop was in a suitcase somewhere in London. He called the airport at once, but a recorded voice told him that the office was closed until seven o'clock. Then he had an idea. He found the telephone number of the hotel in Milan on the label and called it. A sleepy man answered in Italian, and Daniel did not understand a single word.

At six in the morning, Daniel took a taxi back to the airport with the red dress in his arms. He felt a little ridiculous, and the taxi driver gave him a strange look in the mirror. At the lost luggage desk, a friendly woman called Joan checked her computer. "Yes," she said, "I have a message about a blue suitcase. A lady has been waiting here since last night. She is very angry."

Carla Rossi was a tall woman with bright eyes and a loud voice. She stood near the desk with Daniel's suitcase beside her, and she was wearing the same clothes as the day before. "Is this yours?" she asked, pointing at his blue case. "Because I have your shirts, your jeans, and a very boring computer. And you have my dress!" Daniel nodded. For a moment, they looked at each other, and then both of them started laughing, because the situation was so silly.

They exchanged the suitcases, and Carla explained her problem. She was a wedding planner, and she was flying to London to organise a big wedding that afternoon. The red dress was her own, and she was going to wear it at the party. "If I lost this dress," she said, "I would lose my job and my dignity." Daniel looked at his watch. It was seven o'clock, and his presentation began at nine. He needed to hurry, but he also felt hungry, so he asked her to join him for a quick breakfast.

They sat in the airport cafe and ate eggs and toast. Carla told him that she hated flying, and that she always packed too many shoes. Daniel told her about his job, which was to design computer games for children. His presentation was about a new game with a friendly dragon. "A dragon who loves vegetables?" Carla asked. "My nephew would adore that!" He opened his laptop, and she listened to the whole presentation twice, and she gave him several good ideas.

The presentation went very well. The managers at the company laughed at the dragon, and one of them asked to see the game immediately. Daniel did not mention the dress, and he did not mention the sweets, and he did not say that he had practised the speech in front of a stranger in a cafe. At lunchtime, he sent a short message to Carla through the airport office. He thanked her for her ideas and wished her a perfect wedding.

Three weeks later, a parcel arrived at his flat in Toronto. Inside was a box of Italian chocolates and a card with a photograph of a bride and groom. The groom held a small blue suitcase, and the bride had a big smile on her face. On the back, Carla wrote: "Next time, buy a green one! But please do not forget to write to me about the dragon." Daniel bought a green suitcase the next day, and he put a bright yellow ribbon on the handle, just in case.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Язык между зубами, как для θ, но с голосом; звук мягкий и звонкий, не «з» и не «д».
Язык не касается нёба и не вибрирует; кончик слегка загнут назад, губы чуть округлены.
Короткий расслабленный звук между «и» и «ы»; не тяните его и не смягчайте предыдущую согласную.

questions.question: What city did Daniel fly from?
What was in the wrong suitcase?
questions.answer: A red dress, shoes, sweets and an Italian book.

questions.question: What did Carla send to Daniel later?
questions.answer: A parcel with chocolates and a card.
